name: Braun Silk-expert IPL

lead: Braun Silk-expert is a home intense pulsed light (IPL) line used for at-home hair reduction, with versions that use a skin-tone sensor to adjust or block flashes. The goal is less visible body hair over repeated sessions.

Pulsed light is absorbed by melanin in the hair and heats the follicle, so follicles weaken over multiple sessions. Home IPL as a category has trial support for hair reduction; trials specific to this line were not found.

paras: Users flash the device over shaved skin in sessions repeated over weeks, then do occasional maintenance. It works best on darker hair, and manufacturers restrict use to light-to-medium skin tones.
Burns, redness and pigmentation changes are reported with IPL, and light-based removal is limited by skin tone and hair colour. Eye safety is a design concern with home IPL.

angle.text: Users choose Braun Silk-expert IPL for at-home hair reduction. Light pulses target hair pigment and weaken follicles over repeated sessions, leaving less visible body hair. Home IPL has trial support as a category; trials specific to this line are not found.

lead: Braun Silk-expert is Braun's home intense pulsed light (IPL) hair-removal line, with versions described as having a skin-tone sensor. People use home IPL to reduce body or facial hair at home, aiming for smoother skin and a clean-shaven face without repeated shaving or salon visits. Braun is a Procter & Gamble subsidiary, and Wikipedia lists IPL appliances and epilators among its beauty-care products [1].

IPL uses broad-spectrum light that is absorbed by melanin, travels down the hair shaft and heats the follicle; only hairs in the active growth phase respond, so repeated sessions are needed, typically around 8 to 10 spaced 4 to 6 weeks apart, according to Wikipedia [2]. It reports that IPL permanently reduces the number of hairs without removing all of them, and that it works best on darker, coarser hair [2]. Wikipedia cites manufacturer statements that such devices suit light to medium skin tones [2].

A male user's account of the Braun Silk-Expert Pro 5, cross-posted to a Lemmy community, circulated as an alternative to expensive salon laser visits [3]. No device-specific clinical studies were found, so this entry is brief.
infobox: About 8 to 10 treatments, 4 to 6 weeks apart [2]
Works best on darker hair; light to medium skin tones [2]

paras: Braun was founded by Max Braun in Frankfurt in 1921, was acquired by Gillette in stages from 1967, and became a Procter & Gamble subsidiary when P&G acquired Gillette in 2005.[1]

Clinic IPL studies have reported hair reduction of roughly half to two-thirds at six to twelve months; side effects include redness, burns and pigment changes [2][4]. A 2006 comparison cited by Wikipedia found about 67 percent hair reduction at six months with IPL versus about 69 percent for alexandrite and 72 percent for diode lasers, with temporary side effects in 15.3 percent of IPL patients [2]. In one trial at 12 months, diode laser reduced hair by 69.2 percent versus 52.7 percent for IPL [4]. These data do not come from Braun devices.

The FDA defines permanent hair reduction as a long-term, stable reduction in regrowing hairs rather than total removal, and many patients regrow hair years after their last session [4]. Laser works best on light skin with dark coarse hair, and white, grey, red or light blonde hair responds poorly [4].
Shimon Eckhouse invented IPL in 1992; ESC Medical commercialised it, and the FDA cleared it for vascular lesions in 1995, pigmented lesions in 1996 and hair removal in 1997 [2].
